items.stem: Using the hierarchy of controls, the MOST preferred way to deal with a fall hazard at an unprotected edge is to:

options.text: Eliminate the hazard or redesign the task so the edge exposure is removed
options.rationale: Correct: elimination/design-out sits at the top of the hierarchy.

options.text: Issue harnesses and rely on PPE
options.rationale: PPE is the least preferred control, used when higher controls are not feasible.
Administrative signage alone does not remove the hazard.
Relying on behaviour is the weakest control.

items.explanation: Correct: elimination/design-out sits at the top of the hierarchy.

items.stem: The main reason to investigate a near-miss is to:

options.text: Find and fix the causes before an actual injury occurs
options.rationale: Correct: near-misses reveal causes that can be corrected proactively.
A near-miss does not automatically close a site.

items.explanation: Correct: near-misses reveal causes that can be corrected proactively.

items.stem: Select TWO controls that rank ABOVE personal protective equipment in the hierarchy of controls.

options.rationale: Correct: engineering controls rank above PPE.
A hard hat is PPE, the lowest tier.

items.explanation: Correct: engineering controls rank above PPE. Correct: substitution ranks above PPE.
